section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Capture repository identity and revision
preconditions: Local Antigravity workspace is open.
steps: Run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git branch --show-current`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git status --short`. Save the outputs before running tests.
expected_result: Repository root, branch, commit SHA, and dirty-file list are recorded; no existing work is discarded.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Preserve uncommitted implementation changes
preconditions: Workspace may contain uncommitted remediation.
steps: Review `git status --short` and `git diff --stat`; do not checkout, reset, clean, stash, or overwrite files unless the owner explicitly directs it.
expected_result: All pre-existing modifications remain intact; test outputs are placed in a dedicated artifacts folder.
evidence: Before/after git status and diff stat.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Verify claimed report and CI files exist in workspace
preconditions: Post-remediation report claims the files were created.
steps: Check the exact paths `CCIP_FINAL_PRODUCTION_READINESS_REPORT.md` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; inspect their contents and timestamps.
expected_result: Files exist in the active workspace and content matches the reported implementation; if missing, record discrepancy without fabricating success.
evidence: File paths, content excerpt, git status.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Check workspace versus remote snapshot drift
preconditions: Git remote is configured.
steps: Record `git remote -v`; compare current branch/HEAD and relevant changed paths against remote tracking branch, without pulling or switching branches.
expected_result: It is clear whether remediation is local/uncommitted, committed locally, or present remotely; no automatic synchronization occurs.
evidence: HEAD SHAs; `git diff <remote>/<branch>...HEAD --stat`; note remote status.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Confirm isolated test environment
preconditions: Test configuration is available.
steps: Inspect effective environment variable names and test DB/cache/storage endpoints without printing secret values. Confirm the app cannot point at production resources.
expected_result: Tests target an isolated test database and test storage; secret values are not written to logs or artifacts.
evidence: Redacted config summary; test DB name/host.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Confirm safe test-data policy
preconditions: Test fixtures can be created.
steps: Search fixture data and test scripts for real citizen PII, real credentials, production endpoints, or genuine evidence files. Replace any accidental real data with synthetic values.
expected_result: Only synthetic test identities and files are used; no real cases or user data are changed.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Verify deterministic test execution instructions
preconditions: Dependencies are installed in the workspace.
steps: Read `pyproject.toml`/requirements, frontend package scripts, pytest configuration, and README instructions. Resolve exact commands from current repository rather than assuming these docs are current.
expected_result: Each planned command is supported by this checkout and its runtime; absent dependencies are reported as blockers.

section: A. Baseline, test safety, and repository truth
title: Record test environment/version metadata
preconditions: Test runner is available.
steps: Capture OS, Python version, Node/npm version, browser versions, database version, Redis/storage state, and model artifact inventory. Redact secrets.
expected_result: A reproducible environment manifest is saved with the run.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Valid login succeeds
preconditions: Active test user exists for each supported role.
steps: Submit valid credentials through the supported login API/UI.
expected_result: A session/token is issued with the intended identity and role; no password or secret appears in response/logs.
evidence: Redacted response; status code; UI screenshot.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Invalid password is rejected
preconditions: Active test account exists.
steps: Submit correct identifier with an incorrect password.
expected_result: Authentication fails with generic safe error; no token/session is created and no user existence leak is introduced.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Unknown account login is rejected safely
preconditions: No account exists for synthetic email.
steps: Attempt login with the nonexistent identifier.
expected_result: Authentication fails without exposing account-enumeration details beyond approved policy.
evidence: Response comparison for unknown vs wrong password.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Missing credential fields are rejected
preconditions: Login endpoint is reachable.
steps: Send request with missing username/email, missing password, empty strings, and malformed body.
expected_result: Validation rejects invalid bodies predictably; no traceback or 500 response.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Inactive or disabled account cannot authenticate
preconditions: Create a disabled test account.
steps: Attempt login with correct credentials.
expected_result: Login is denied and no active session is issued.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Expired access token is rejected
preconditions: Obtain a token with controlled short expiry or use a safe expired fixture.
steps: Call a protected endpoint after expiration.
expected_result: Request is denied with the documented authentication status; protected data is not returned.
evidence: Request/response and token metadata with secret redacted.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Tampered token signature is rejected
preconditions: A valid test token is available.
steps: Change one token byte/claim without signing and call protected endpoint.
expected_result: Request is rejected; no identity or privilege escalation occurs.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Token claim tampering does not elevate role
preconditions: Role-based tokens are in use.
steps: Attempt to alter role/user ID claims in a token without the signing key.
expected_result: Tampered token is rejected; server-side role is not trusted from unsigned client input.
evidence: Request/response and relevant auth implementation reference.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Logout invalidates session when designed to do so
preconditions: Logged-in test user and logout path exist.
steps: Logout; then replay token/session against a protected endpoint.
expected_result: Session is invalidated according to the documented strategy; if JWTs are stateless, documented expiry/revocation behavior is verified instead.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Refresh token rotation/reuse behavior
preconditions: Refresh flow exists and test client has a refresh token.
steps: Refresh once; attempt reuse of prior refresh token; replay the new token.
expected_result: Refresh policy is enforced, old-token reuse is rejected if rotation is specified, and token values are never logged.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Password reset or OTP flow boundary checks
preconditions: Password recovery/OTP is enabled in this deployment.
steps: Test wrong OTP, expired OTP, reused OTP, too many attempts, and successful one-time use with test provider.
expected_result: Invalid/replayed codes fail, expiry/cooldown is enforced, and success changes only the intended account.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: OAuth callback validates state and redirect
preconditions: Google OAuth is configured for a test client.
steps: Test valid callback, missing/invalid state, invalid code, and unapproved redirect URI.
expected_result: Only valid flow completes; state/redirect validation blocks CSRF/open-redirect paths.
evidence: Callback requests and config with secrets redacted.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Authentication errors do not leak secrets
preconditions: Auth logs and error middleware are observable in test environment.
steps: Trigger invalid credentials and malformed auth token; inspect client response and logs.
expected_result: No password, full token, OTP, API key, or secret appears in response/logs.

section: B. Authentication, sessions, and identity lifecycle
title: Rate limit or abuse controls on authentication
preconditions: Test environment has auth abuse controls enabled.
steps: Submit a controlled series of failed logins from a test client within the configured window.
expected_result: Rate limits/lockout/step-up policy triggers as documented without locking unrelated users.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Anonymous caller cannot read protected case
preconditions: A case with synthetic data exists.
steps: Call case list and direct case detail APIs with no token.
expected_result: Both are denied; no case or linked complaint data is returned.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Citizen cannot read another citizen case
preconditions: Citizen A and Citizen B have separate synthetic complaints/cases.
steps: Login as A; request B case by internal ID and case number.
expected_result: Access is denied or resource is consistently hidden per policy; B data is not disclosed.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Citizen cannot use list filters to enumerate others
preconditions: Multiple synthetic users/cases exist.
steps: As citizen, vary case IDs, complaint IDs, status, priority, and pagination/filter values.
expected_result: Only authorized personal records are returned; total counts do not leak inaccessible records.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Unassigned staff cannot read restricted case
preconditions: Case has assignment to Staff A; Staff B has same broad role but no assignment.
steps: As B, request case detail through every alias/identifier and any linked complaint route.
expected_result: Object-level case policy is enforced consistently on each endpoint.
evidence: API results for IDs, case number, linked resource.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Assigned specialist reads permitted case
preconditions: Specialist A is explicitly assigned to a synthetic case.
steps: Request case detail and approved linked evidence/complaint fields.
expected_result: Only the scope approved for that specialist is returned; required operational fields remain usable.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Specialist cannot change assignment or privilege
preconditions: Specialist has access to one case.
steps: Attempt to assign another staff member, alter role, change protected case fields, and call admin-only endpoints.
expected_result: Forbidden operations fail; no partial mutation occurs.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Police/investigator access follows assignment policy
preconditions: Two officers with distinct assignments exist.
steps: Run identical read/write operations on assigned and unassigned cases under both accounts.
expected_result: Only operations allowed by role and assignment policy succeed.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Administrator rights are intentional and audited
preconditions: Admin test account exists.
steps: Perform an approved administrative user/role/assignment action.
expected_result: Action succeeds only via approved admin path and creates an audit record.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: AI/ML System Lead cannot read raw citizen narrative by default
preconditions: Complaint includes unique synthetic canary text and identifiable-looking fake fields.
steps: As AI/ML System Lead, inspect case list/detail, model endpoints, correlation data, logs, report preview, and exports.
expected_result: Narrative is masked or withheld on all restricted paths; no canary/raw content leaks unless an explicit, approved, audited permission grants it.
evidence: Response field scan; UI screenshots; logs.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Narrative masking occurs server-side before model call
preconditions: A test instrument can capture model inputs in a local test adapter.
steps: Submit synthetic complaint with fake name/email/phone and canary token; trigger AI triage.
expected_result: Model adapter receives masked/minimized text before the network/model boundary, not merely a masked UI rendering.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Report access inherits case permission
preconditions: Report A relates to case A; user cannot access case A.
steps: Attempt report metadata, detail, preview, export/download, and report generation referencing case A.
expected_result: All paths consistently deny access; report IDs cannot be used to bypass case permission.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Evidence read/download inherits complaint/case permission
preconditions: Evidence A belongs to protected complaint/case A.
steps: As unauthorized user, request evidence metadata, processing status, download, and direct object/storage path if exposed.
expected_result: All unauthorized paths fail without revealing file bytes, hash, filename, or sensitive metadata beyond approved denial details.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Evidence processing actions require authority
preconditions: Evidence A exists; caller is authenticated but unassigned/role-restricted.
steps: Invoke processing/reprocess/cancel/verify endpoints where available.
expected_result: Unauthorized actions are rejected and processing state remains unchanged.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Role cannot be changed through request payload
preconditions: Citizen and staff test users exist.
steps: Submit registration/profile update payloads containing role/admin flags or user IDs for another person.
expected_result: Protected role/identity fields are ignored or rejected; persisted role remains unchanged.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Role-scoped model operations deny disallowed role
preconditions: AI model endpoints exist.
steps: Call each model inference/management route under citizen, specialist, police, and admin roles.
expected_result: Allowed matrix is enforced consistently; no hidden inference route bypasses checks.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Cross-case correlation review requires authorized reviewer
preconditions: Correlation candidate links two cases; user is not permitted to review one or both.
steps: Attempt to approve, reject, mark duplicate, edit relation, or force refresh candidate.
expected_result: Disallowed review/update operations fail without changing decision or case data.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Direct object IDs cannot bypass API scoping
preconditions: IDs and case numbers for inaccessible records are known in a safe test fixture.
steps: Replace visible IDs in URLs and JSON bodies with inaccessible IDs across read/write endpoints.
expected_result: Every endpoint performs authorization at object access; no IDOR.

section: C. Role-based access control and object-level authorization
title: Authorization failure has no side effect
preconditions: Prepare target record and snapshot its relevant fields.
steps: Attempt a forbidden write or state transition; compare DB and audit events.
expected_result: No unauthorized mutation or misleading success audit is created.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Citizen submits valid complaint
preconditions: Citizen is authenticated or an explicitly approved guest submission path is configured.
steps: Submit complaint with valid title, description, category, contact consent, and only required fields.
expected_result: Complaint is stored once, receives stable reference/state, and displays truthful confirmation.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Guest complaint flow matches documented policy
preconditions: Guest intake is intended by product design or is explicitly disabled.
steps: Submit without a login; verify required guest verification/consent controls and record ownership strategy.
expected_result: Guest submission is either correctly supported with safe anti-abuse/ownership controls or rejected if guest intake is not allowed; no invented citizen identity is silently treated as verified.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Required fields are enforced
preconditions: Complaint form/API is available.
steps: Submit with each required field missing, empty, null, whitespace, and invalid type.
expected_result: Validation explains correctable errors and writes no incomplete complaint.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Length and boundary validation
preconditions: Complaint schemas and limits are discoverable.
steps: Test min/max lengths, one character below/above bounds, Unicode, newline, and large body.
expected_result: Inputs inside policy bounds persist accurately; out-of-range inputs fail safely without 500 or truncation surprises.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Malicious markup is safely rendered
preconditions: A complaint can be viewed in a UI.
steps: Submit escaped HTML/script/event-handler payloads in title and narrative; open all relevant views.
expected_result: Payload is rendered as text or safely sanitized; no script executes and no stored/reflected XSS occurs.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Duplicate submit does not create accidental duplicate
preconditions: Complaint form/API allows submit.
steps: Double-click submit and replay the same request using supported idempotency behavior.
expected_result: UI prevents accidental double submission; backend behavior is deterministic and dedupe is applied when the contract supports it.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Complaint reference is unique under concurrency
preconditions: Test DB only; reference creation is supported.
steps: Create a burst of synthetic complaints concurrently and check unique constraint/collision handling.
expected_result: No two persisted complaints share a reference; conflicts are retried or returned safely.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Status transition follows allowed state graph
preconditions: Complaint lifecycle transitions are documented from current code.
steps: Attempt each allowed transition and representative disallowed jumps through UI/API.
expected_result: Only permitted transitions occur; invalid transition is rejected with no partial update.
evidence: Transition matrix and DB audit trail.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Complaint status persists after reload
preconditions: Complaint has moved to a new state.
steps: Reload UI and query the backing API after a fresh session/request.
expected_result: Persisted status/timestamps match the successful operation.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Citizen sees own complaint only
preconditions: Two citizen users own distinct complaints.
steps: Login as A and query list/detail/search/timeline for B.
expected_result: No B record or metadata leaks.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Citizen complaint edits are limited by lifecycle
preconditions: Complaint exists in pre- and post-review states.
steps: Attempt permitted edits before review and prohibited edits after lifecycle lock.
expected_result: Edits are limited exactly as policy specifies and audit history records permitted changes.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Complaint category/severity values validated
preconditions: Valid enum values are confirmed in schema/UI.
steps: Submit valid category/severity and unknown, lower/upper-case, forged risk/triage values.
expected_result: Only allowed client-supplied fields are accepted; server-calculated fields cannot be spoofed.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Triage fallback is truthful
preconditions: Model unavailable mode can be simulated safely.
steps: Submit synthetic complaint while classifier service/assets are unavailable.
expected_result: Complaint intake remains available if designed to; triage is identified as fallback/unavailable and does not claim neural inference occurred.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Attachment relationship is complaint-bound
preconditions: Two synthetic complaints and their upload sessions exist.
steps: Try attaching evidence via another complaint ID and change request fields between upload and submission.
expected_result: Evidence belongs only to authorized intended complaint; mismatched relationship is rejected.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Concurrent status updates do not silently overwrite
preconditions: Two test staff accounts can update a synthetic complaint.
steps: Read same state in two sessions and attempt concurrent conflicting transitions.
expected_result: Conflict/ordering behavior is deterministic; invalid stale update is reported or versioned safely.

section: D. Citizen complaint intake and lifecycle
title: Complaint deletion/retention follows policy
preconditions: Retention/deletion controls exist or policy specifies no physical delete.
steps: Attempt citizen delete, admin delete, and retention expiry in test data.
expected_result: Only authorized policy-supported action occurs; evidence/audit dependencies and legal hold rules are respected.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Tracking requires appropriate verification
preconditions: Complaint and its high-entropy tracking credential exist in test DB.
steps: Request the tracking endpoint with reference only and with valid reference plus token.
expected_result: Unauthenticated detail/status exposure follows explicit policy; detailed/trusted data requires valid verification token where designed.
evidence: Response field inventory for both variants.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Wrong tracking token is rejected
preconditions: Known synthetic reference exists.
steps: Submit wrong token, truncated token, and token for another complaint.
expected_result: Verification fails without exposing protected status or confirming a valid token.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Tracking token cannot be guessed from reference
preconditions: At least one synthetic tracking reference exists.
steps: Inspect token generation and issue low-volume bounded guesses with test rate limit.
expected_result: Token is high entropy, not derived from reference; guessing attempts are limited and audited.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Reference enumeration is rate-limited
preconditions: Tracking endpoint uses synthetic records only.
steps: Issue controlled sequence of invalid refs from a test client.
expected_result: Abuse controls apply; responses do not leak whether refs are valid beyond approved policy.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Public tracking response minimizes data
preconditions: Complaint contains synthetic PII/narrative/evidence filename.
steps: Fetch public tracking response with permitted credential; inspect all nested fields.
expected_result: No raw narrative, contact details, evidence URLs, internal IDs, assignments, notes, or investigator identities leak unless explicitly approved.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Tracking token storage/use is safe
preconditions: DB schema and service are accessible in test.
steps: Inspect storage/transmission approach and logs; exercise token in query/body/header as designed.
expected_result: Token does not appear in logs/analytics/referrer; storage follows declared threat model and token values are not returned casually.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Tracking token rotates or revokes if supported
preconditions: Token rotation/revocation policy exists.
steps: Rotate/revoke a test token and replay old token.
expected_result: Old token no longer verifies if rotation/revocation is promised.

section: E. Complaint tracking and reference protection
title: Tracking UI handles invalid and expired state
preconditions: Tracking screen exists.
steps: Enter malformed reference, wrong token, expired token (if applicable), and valid values.
expected_result: Accessible, non-enumerating error is shown; no stale data remains on screen after failure.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Authorized staff creates case from complaint
preconditions: Validated synthetic complaint exists and actor has required role.
steps: Invoke create-from-complaint once.
expected_result: One case links to the complaint, correct fields are populated, and an audit/timeline record is created.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case creation is idempotent
preconditions: Complaint has a case or is eligible for case creation.
steps: Call create-from-complaint repeatedly and concurrently.
expected_result: Exactly one official case remains linked to the complaint; retries do not create duplicate cases.
evidence: DB uniqueness query and concurrent test.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case detail endpoint enforces object scope
preconditions: Case assigned to Staff A; Staff B unauthorized.
steps: As B call detail by internal ID, external case number, and alternate accepted identifier.
expected_result: All identifiers enforce the same object authorization policy.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case list is scoped by assignment/policy
preconditions: Cases are assigned to distinct staff and departments.
steps: Query default case list, all filters, assigned-to-me true/false, and pagination.
expected_result: Default query cannot expose unassigned/inaccessible cases; filter toggles cannot bypass scope.
evidence: API response IDs vs expected access set.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Assignment requires authorized role
preconditions: Case and candidate users exist.
steps: Attempt assignment as citizen, unauthorized specialist, assigned staff, and admin as policy allows.
expected_result: Only authorized assignment operations succeed.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Assignment target must be valid and eligible
preconditions: A case and user IDs exist; include nonexistent and wrong-role users.
steps: Assign nonexistent, disabled, citizen, or ineligible user.
expected_result: Invalid assignments are rejected without corrupting relationship.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Assignment change is audited
preconditions: Actor can assign case.
steps: Change assignment from Staff A to Staff B.
expected_result: Previous and new assignee, actor, time, and case are traceable in audit history.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Unauthorized case status transition is rejected
preconditions: Case status graph and role permissions are known.
steps: Attempt status changes as each role, including invalid transitions.
expected_result: Only allowed actors/transitions succeed; no partial state or misleading UI success.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Priority/risk values cannot be forged
preconditions: Case exists.
steps: Submit impossible priority/risk scores and client-supplied risk flags.
expected_result: Server validates or recalculates protected fields; unauthorized arbitrary risk changes fail.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case reopen/close requires reason and permission
preconditions: Case is closed/resolved in test fixture.
steps: Attempt reopen/close with no reason, invalid reason, and valid reason as roles.
expected_result: Policy is enforced and reopening creates a visible history/audit record.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case status history is append-only/traceable
preconditions: Multiple valid transitions completed.
steps: Query status history, compare actor/time/order, attempt alteration where endpoint exists.
expected_result: Historical transitions remain ordered and protected against ordinary mutation.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Investigation activity creation is scoped
preconditions: Case assigned to investigator A.
steps: Create activity/note as A then attempt as unrelated user; try forged actor ID.
expected_result: Allowed activity persists with authenticated actor; unauthorized insert is rejected and actor cannot be spoofed.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Investigation finding links to source evidence
preconditions: Evidence and case are valid and authorized.
steps: Create finding referencing evidence; then attempt foreign case/evidence ID.
expected_result: Valid finding preserves traceability; invalid relationship is rejected.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Cross-case action cannot silently modify source case
preconditions: Correlation candidate connects cases A/B.
steps: Review/refresh correlation, then compare source-case status/assignment and audit data.
expected_result: Correlation action does not make unapproved changes to cases; all side effects are explicit and audited.

section: F. Case management, assignment, and investigation workflow
title: Case data persists across process restart
preconditions: A test case and investigation activity have been created.
steps: Restart only the test app process; retrieve case and activity again.
expected_result: Durable data remains available and consistent.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Unauthenticated upload is denied or tightly scoped
preconditions: Evidence upload endpoint and guest policy are confirmed from current code/design.
steps: Attempt upload with no credentials; then test the documented guest-upload credential if such a path exists.
expected_result: Anonymous upload is rejected unless a deliberate, narrowly scoped guest capability exists; no anonymous arbitrary complaint attachment is allowed.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Authenticated uploader must own or be authorized for complaint
preconditions: Complaints A/B belong to separate test citizens.
steps: Upload to own complaint; then use same user/session to upload to another citizen’s complaint.
expected_result: Own authorized upload succeeds; cross-citizen upload is denied with no stored evidence row/object.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: File type allowlist enforced server-side
preconditions: Evidence upload accepts test files.
steps: Try allowed document/image/archive formats and disallowed executable/script/unknown extensions with spoofed MIME.
expected_result: Policy is enforced using server-side content/extension checks; dangerous files are rejected or quarantined.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: File size boundary enforced
preconditions: Configured upload limit is identified.
steps: Upload just below, at, and above max size; also send oversized chunked request if supported.
expected_result: Accepted sizes follow configuration; oversize uploads fail before excessive resource use.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Filename traversal and special names are neutralized
preconditions: Upload endpoint active.
steps: Use `../`, absolute paths, Unicode separators, long filenames, reserved device names, and CRLF characters.
expected_result: Storage path is generated safely; original display name is escaped/normalized; no filesystem traversal or header injection.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: SHA-256 matches received bytes
preconditions: Use a known synthetic file with known bytes.
steps: Upload file; independently compute SHA-256 of original bytes and compare API/DB digest.
expected_result: Digest exactly matches the uploaded byte stream and is consistent wherever displayed.
evidence: Computed hash; API response; DB row.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Evidence bytes cannot be changed without detection
preconditions: Evidence is stored with integrity hash.
steps: In isolated test storage, mutate stored bytes; download/verify.
expected_result: Integrity verification detects mismatch and marks/reports evidence as tampered or invalid; it does not claim verified.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Malware-infected file is rejected/quarantined
preconditions: ClamAV or test scanner adapter is available in non-production test.
steps: Upload the standard EICAR test string/file, not real malware.
expected_result: File is blocked or quarantined; content is not processed/downloaded as clean; event is auditable.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Scanner unavailable produces explicit NOT_SCANNED state
preconditions: Use test adapter or stop only the isolated scanner service.
steps: Upload harmless synthetic file while scan service is unreachable.
expected_result: State is NOT_SCANNED/QUARANTINED per policy; UI never marks scan as passed or verified clean.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Unscanned files are not processed as trusted
preconditions: Evidence in NOT_SCANNED state exists.
steps: Attempt OCR/parser/AI extraction, export, and ordinary download.
expected_result: Unscanned evidence is blocked or limited to explicit safe/quarantined handling; no downstream processor runs as if clean.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Scanner clean verdict is distinguished from integrity digest
preconditions: Harmless file and online scanner are available.
steps: Upload clean file and inspect verification fields.
expected_result: Hash integrity, malware verdict, forensic verification, and human validation remain distinct concepts; no field conflates them.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Malformed or empty file is handled safely
preconditions: Upload endpoint active.
steps: Upload zero-byte file, corrupt PDF, invalid image, malformed archive, and incorrect MIME.
expected_result: File is rejected or stored in explicit invalid state; parser exceptions do not cause 500 or leave partial objects.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Evidence metadata is owner/role scoped
preconditions: Evidence A is attached to a protected complaint.
steps: Call metadata endpoint as owner, authorized staff, and unrelated citizen.
expected_result: Response follows policy; inaccessible metadata is not disclosed.

section: G. Evidence upload, quarantine, processing, integrity, and download
title: Evidence download rechecks authorization
preconditions: A valid download URL exists.
steps: Access as owner/authorized staff then replay URL as unrelated user and without token.
expected_result: Download endpoint reauthorizes every request; URL alone does not become a bearer secret unless explicitly designed and bounded.
